The task: add a `save()` method to `Order` that resolves the repository class from the `ORDER_REPOSITORY` string setting at runtime (lazy import inside the method), instantiates it, and calls `repo.save(self)`.

The string format is `"module:Class"`. Use `importlib` to import the module, then `getattr` for the class. The import happens inside `save()` so no top-level import of `shop.infrastructure` is needed.

```python
import importlib
from dataclasses import dataclass

from shop.domain.ports import OrderRepository
from shop.domain.settings import ORDER_REPOSITORY


@dataclass
class Order:
    id: str
    total_cents: int

    def save(self) -> None:
        module_name, class_name = ORDER_REPOSITORY.split(":")
        repo_class = getattr(importlib.import_module(module_name), class_name)
        repo_class().save(self)
```

One consideration: should the method name conflict with the repo's `save`? No issue — `Order.save` is on the domain object, `repo.save(order)` is the port method. That's the intended design.

21: const CONFIG = /(^|[\\/])pyproject\.toml$/iu;
22: /** A command that names one of those files, or the config. */
23: const MENTIONS = /pyproject\.toml|\.opencode|opencode\.jsonc?|\.inwards|inwards-baseline/iu;
24: /**
25:  * A patch header, read at least as leniently as OpenCode reads it. OpenCode
26:  * splits a patch on "\n" only, so the path runs to that: a "\r" or a Unicode
27:  * line separator inside it is part of the path, and it is trimmed as
28:  * OpenCode trims it.
29:  */
30: const PATCH_FILE = /^\s*\*\*\*\s*(?:(?:Add|Update|Delete)\s+File|Move\s+to)\s*:(?<path>[^\n]*)$/iu;
31: /** Inwards' own files and this plugin, by where they are in the project; links to them count too. */
32: const OWN_FILES = [".opencode", ".inwards", "inwards-baseline.json", "opencode.json", "opencode.jsonc"];
33: /** Marks the messages the plugin sends, so they don't count as the user's. */
34: const OWN = "(sent by the Inwards plugin, not the user)";
35: const STOP_PREFACE = `Inwards Stop gate ${OWN}: the turn can't end yet. Fix what follows, then finish your turn.\n\n`;
36: const NOTE_PREFACE = `Inwards ${OWN}: `;
37: /** How many links to follow by hand before giving up on a path. */
38: const MAX_LINKS = 40;
39: /** How long one hook run may take, as Claude Code's default hook timeout. */
40: const HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS = 60000;
41: 
42: /**
43:  * Runs the hook with one payload, in the project init wrote the plugin into.
44:  *
45:  * @param payload - a hook payload, as Claude Code would send it.
46:  * @returns the exit code and both output streams; code -1 when Inwards couldn't start or was stopped.
47:  */
48: async function hook(payload) {
49:   try {
50:     const proc = Bun.spawn([...INWARDS, "hook", "claude-code"], {
51:       cwd: PROJECT,
52:       stdin: new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify({ cwd: PROJECT, ...payload })),
53:       stdout: "pipe",
54:       stderr: "pipe",
55:       timeout: HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS,
56:       env: {
57:         ...process.env,
58:         CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR: PROJECT,
59:         INWARDS_HOOK_HOST: "opencode",
60:         INWARDS_PLUGIN_SHA256: SELF,
61:       },
62:     });
63:     const [stdout, stderr, code] = await Promise.all([
64:       new Response(proc.stdout).text(),
65:       new Response(proc.stderr).text(),
66:       proc.exited,
67:     ]);
68:     return proc.signalCode
69:       ? { code: -1, stdout, stderr: `inwards: stopped (${proc.signalCode}); a hook run may take ${HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS / 1000} s` }
70:       : { code, stdout, stderr };
71:   } catch (err) {
72:     return { code: -1, stdout: "", stderr: `inwards: ${String(err)}` };
73:   }
74: }
75: 
76: /**
77:  * Tells whether the hook failed instead of answering: it couldn't start, or
78:  * exited with neither 0 nor 2.
79:  *
80:  * @param result - what `hook` returned.
81:  * @returns true when nothing was checked.
82:  */
83: function broken(result) {
84:   return result.code !== 0 && result.code !== 2;
85: }
86: 
87: /**
88:  * Reads a field of the hook's JSON output.
89:  *
90:  * @param stdout - the hook's output.
91:  * @returns the parsed object, or an empty one.
92:  */
93: function output(stdout) {
94:   try {
95:     return JSON.parse(stdout) ?? {};
96:   } catch {
97:     return {};
98:   }
99: }
100: 
101: /**
102:  * Reads the reason out of a PreToolUse deny, if the hook denied.
103:  *
104:  * @param stdout - the hook's output.
105:  * @returns the reason (a default when the hook gave none), or undefined when the call may go ahead.
106:  */
107: function denial(stdout) {
108:   const decision = output(stdout).hookSpecificOutput;
109:   if (decision?.permissionDecision !== "deny") {
110:     return undefined;
111:   }
112:   return decision.permissionDecisionReason || "Inwards refused this call.";
113: }
114: 
115: /**
116:  * Resolves links in a path, a dangling one included, so an alias can't hide
117:  * a protected file. A path that doesn't exist yet resolves through its
118:  * nearest existing directory.
119:  *
120:  * @param path - an absolute path.
121:  * @param depth - links followed so far.
122:  * @returns the path with every link resolved that can be.
123:  */
124: function real(path, depth = 0) {
125:   try {
126:     return realpathSync(path);
127:   } catch {
128:     // missing, or a dangling link: go on by hand
129:   }
130:   if (depth > MAX_LINKS) {
131:     return path;
132:   }
133:   try {
134:     return real(resolve(dirname(path), readlinkSync(path)), depth + 1);
135:   } catch {
136:     // not a link
137:   }
138:   const parent = dirname(path);
139:   return parent === path ? path : join(real(parent, depth + 1), basename(path));
140: }
141: 
142: /**
143:  * Tells whether a path, as written or once its links are resolved, matches.
144:  *
145:  * @param pattern - PROTECTED or CONFIG.
146:  * @param path - an absolute path.
147:  * @returns true when either spelling matches.
148:  */
149: function names(pattern, path) {
150:   const p = String(path ?? "");
151:   return pattern.test(p) || pattern.test(real(p));
152: }
153: 
154: /**
155:  * Tells whether a path is, or lies inside, one of the project's own files
156:  * once links on both sides are resolved: \`settings.toml\` when
157:  * \`pyproject.toml\` links to it, say.
158:  *
159:  * @param path - an absolute path.
160:  * @param names - files of the project, relative to it.
161:  * @returns true when the path resolves into one of them.
162:  */
163: function resolvesTo(path, names) {
164:   const target = real(String(path ?? ""));
165:   return names.some((name) => {
166:     const own = real(join(PROJECT, name));
167:     return target === own || target.startsWith(own + sep);
168:   });
169: }
170: 
171: /**
172:  * Tells whether a path is Inwards' own: the plugin, the state, the baseline or OpenCode's config.
173:  *
174:  * @param path - an absolute path.
175:  * @returns true when no tool may change it without the user.
176:  */
177: function inwardsOwn(path) {
178:   return names(PROTECTED, path) || resolvesTo(path, OWN_FILES);
179: }
180: 
181: /**
182:  * Tells whether a path is a pyproject.toml, or a config reached through a
183:  * link: the file a \`pyproject.toml\` in its directory, or any directory
184:  * above it in the project, links to.
185:  *
186:  * @param path - an absolute path.
187:  * @returns true when the config guard must see the change.
188:  */
189: function configFile(path) {
190:   if (names(CONFIG, path) || resolvesTo(path, ["pyproject.toml"])) {
191:     return true;
192:   }
193:   const written = resolve(String(path ?? ""));
194:   const target = real(written);
195:   // The directories above the path as written, and above where it really is.
196:   return [
197:     [dirname(written), resolve(PROJECT)],
198:     [dirname(target), real(PROJECT)],
199:   ].some(([start, top]) => linksFromAbove(start, top, target));
200: }
201: 
202: /**
203:  * Tells whether a pyproject.toml in a directory, or in one above it up to
204:  * the project, links to a file.
205:  *
206:  * @param start - the first directory to look in.
207:  * @param top - the project directory, where the search stops.
208:  * @param target - the file's real path.
209:  * @returns true when one of them resolves to it.
210:  */
211: function linksFromAbove(start, top, target) {
212:   for (let dir = start; dir === top || dir.startsWith(top + sep); dir = dirname(dir)) {
213:     if (real(join(dir, "pyproject.toml")) === target) {
214:       return true;
215:     }
216:     if (dir === top) {
217:       break;
218:     }
219:   }
220:   return false;
221: }

223: /**
224:  * Makes a tool's path absolute, against the directory OpenCode runs in.
225:  *
226:  * @param directory - OpenCode's working directory.
227:  * @param path - the path the tool got.
228:  * @returns the absolute path, or the value as is when it isn't a string.
229:  */
230: function absolute(directory, path) {
231:   return typeof path === "string" && !isAbsolute(path) ? resolve(directory, path) : path;
232: }
233: 
234: /**
235:  * Maps an OpenCode tool's arguments to what the Claude Code tool of the same kind takes.
236:  *
237:  * @param tool - the OpenCode tool.
238:  * @param args - its arguments.
239:  * @param directory - OpenCode's working directory, for relative paths.
240:  * @returns the tool input the hook reads.
241:  */
242: function toolInput(tool, args, directory) {
243:   if (tool === "edit") {
244:     return {
245:       file_path: absolute(directory, args.filePath),
246:       old_string: args.oldString,
247:       new_string: args.newString,
248:       replace_all: args.replaceAll === true,
249:     };
250:   }
251:   if (tool === "write") {
252:     return { file_path: absolute(directory, args.filePath), content: args.content };
253:   }
254:   return { command: args.command };
255: }
256: 
257: /**
258:  * Tells whether OpenCode would change something other than the exact match
259:  * of an edit's oldString. Without exactly one exact match (or one at all,
260:  * with replaceAll) OpenCode tries looser matches: trimmed lines, collapsed
261:  * whitespace, a leading BOM dropped. The config guard simulates the exact,
262:  * normalised match only, so the two could change different lines. The
263:  * guard also drops a leading BOM from both strings and OpenCode doesn't, so
264:  * such an edit is never simulated as written.
265:  *
266:  * @param input - the edit's tool input, as the hook reads it.
267:  * @returns true when the edit's target is up to OpenCode's fallbacks.
268:  */
269: function inexact(input) {
270:   const from = String(input.old_string ?? "").replaceAll("\r\n", "\n");
271:   if (from.startsWith("\uFEFF") || String(input.new_string ?? "").startsWith("\uFEFF")) {
272:     return true;
273:   }
274:   if (from === "") {
275:     return false; // creates a file, which the guard simulates
276:   }
277:   let text;
278:   try {
279:     // As OpenCode reads it: the BOM dropped, then the text matched as is.
280:     text = readFileSync(input.file_path, "utf8").replace(/^\uFEFF/u, "").replaceAll("\r\n", "\n");
281:   } catch {
282:     return false; // a missing file: the guard denies what it can't simulate
283:   }
284:   const first = text.indexOf(from);
285:   if (first === -1) {
286:     return true;
287:   }
288:   return !input.replace_all && text.lastIndexOf(from) !== first;
289: }
290: 
291: /**
292:  * Lists the files an apply_patch call touches.
293:  *
294:  * @param text - the patch.
295:  * @param directory - OpenCode's working directory.
296:  * @returns absolute paths.
297:  */
298: function patchedFiles(text, directory) {
299:   return String(text ?? "")
300:     .split("\n")
301:     .map((line) => PATCH_FILE.exec(line)?.groups?.path?.trim() ?? "")
302:     .filter((path) => path !== "")
303:     .map((path) => absolute(directory, path));
304: }
305: 
306: /**
307:  * Tells whether a tool call reaches the config or Inwards' own files.
308:  *
309:  * @param tool - the OpenCode tool.
310:  * @param input - its tool input, as the hook reads it.
311:  * @returns true when a failed hook must not let it through.
312:  */
313: function touchesRules(tool, input) {
314:   if (tool === "bash") {
315:     return MENTIONS.test(String(input.command ?? ""));
316:   }
317:   return configFile(input.file_path) || inwardsOwn(input.file_path);
318: }
319: 
320: /**
321:  * Tells whether a message is one the plugin sent, and which kind.
322:  *
323:  * @param parts - the message's parts.
324:  * @returns "stop" for the Stop gate's, "note" for another, or undefined for the user's.
325:  */
326: function ownMessage(parts) {
327:   const text = (parts ?? []).map((p) => (typeof p?.text === "string" ? p.text : "")).join("");
328:   if (text.startsWith(STOP_PREFACE)) {
329:     return "stop";
330:   }
331:   return text.startsWith(NOTE_PREFACE) ? "note" : undefined;
332: }
333: 
334: /** How many times a session lookup, or the Stop gate's message, is tried before giving up for now. */
335: const ATTEMPTS = 3;
336: 
337: export const Inwards = async ({ client, directory }) => {
338:   /**
339:    * What the plugin knows about each top-level session:
340:    * - whether the Stop gate sent it back to work, whether that message is still
341:    *   on its way or couldn't be sent, which turn it is (a user's message or
342:    *   the gate's starts one), and which turn the gate is answering;
343:    * - how many messages the user sent, and how many idles came: only the
344:    *   latest idle, from after the user's latest message, runs the gate;
345:    * - whether a turn is running, how many started (a busy status each), and
346:    *   how many had when the gate began its run, and whether one started by a message
347:    *   ended unchecked: an idle after a shell command, a compaction or an
348:    *   abort runs no gate;
349:    * - the agent, model and variant the user picked;
350:    * - how it started, and the queue that runs its Stop checks one at a time.
351:    */
352:   const sessions = new Map();
353:   /** A subagent's session, by the top-level session it works for. */
354:   const parents = new Map();
355:   /** Sessions a message went to while their lookup failed: their next idle runs the gate. */
356:   const unresolved = new Set();
357:   const state = (id) => {
358:     if (!sessions.has(id)) {
359:       sessions.set(id, {
360:         continued: false,
361:         pending: false,
362:         activity: 0,
363:         checked: 0,
364:         awaiting: false,
365:         turn: 0,
366:         running: undefined,
367:         unsent: undefined,
368:         generation: 0,
369:         idles: 0,
370:         busy: false,
371:         starting: undefined,
372:         chosen: {},
373:         queue: Promise.resolve(),
374:       });
375:     }
376:     return sessions.get(id);
377:   };
378: 
379:   /**
380:    * Sends a message into a session. The SDK reports a refused request in its
381:    * result; a thrown error (the connection dropped) leaves unknown whether
382:    * OpenCode took the message.
383:    *
384:    * @param id - the session.
385:    * @param body - the prompt body, without the session's chosen agent and model.
386:    * @returns "sent", "refused", or "unknown" when the request threw.
387:    */
388:   const send = async (id, body) => {
389:     try {
390:       const result = await client.session.promptAsync({ path: { id }, body: { ...state(id).chosen, ...body } });
391:       return result?.error ? "refused" : "sent";
392:     } catch {
393:       return "unknown";
394:     }
395:   };
396: 
397:   /**
398:    * Finds the top-level session a session works for. A subagent's session
399:    * created before OpenCode started is looked up; a failed lookup is tried again next time.
400:    *
401:    * @param id - any session id.
402:    * @returns the id of its top-level session, or undefined while a lookup fails.
403:    */
404:   const root = async (id) => {
405:     if (parents.has(id)) {
406:       return parents.get(id);
407:     }
408:     if (sessions.has(id)) {
409:       return id;
410:     }
411:     let found;
412:     for (let attempt = 0; attempt < ATTEMPTS && !found; attempt += 1) {
413:       try {
414:         const answer = await client.session.get({ path: { id } });
415:         found = answer?.error ? undefined : answer?.data;
416:       } catch {
417:         found = undefined;
418:       }
419:     }
420:     if (!found) {
421:       return undefined;
422:     }
423:     const parentID = found.parentID;
424:     if (parentID) {
425:       const top = await root(parentID);
426:       if (top !== undefined) {
427:         parents.set(id, top);
428:       }
429:       return top;
430:     }
431:     state(id);
432:     return id;
433:   };
434: 
435:   /**
436:    * Records how a top-level session starts, once; every hook of the session
437:    * waits for it. A session OpenCode resumed gets a resume, which only logs itself.
438:    *
439:    * @param id - a top-level session.
440:    * @param source - "startup" for a new session, "resume" otherwise.
441:    * @returns when the record is written.
442:    */
443:   const start = (id, source) => {
444:     const s = state(id);
445:     s.starting ??= (async () => {
446:       const result = await hook({ session_id: id, hook_event_name: "SessionStart", source });
447:       const context = output(result.stdout).hookSpecificOutput?.additionalContext;
448:       if (context) {
449:         await note(id, context);
450:       }
451:     })();
452:     return s.starting;
453:   };
454: 
455:   /**
456:    * Adds a message to a session for the model and the user to read, without
457:    * starting a turn. A turn that is running may still read it.
458:    *
459:    * @param id - the session.
460:    * @param text - what to say.
461:    */
462:   const note = async (id, text) => {
463:     await send(id, { noReply: true, parts: [{ type: "text", text: NOTE_PREFACE + text }] });
464:   };
465: 
466:   /**
467:    * Tells whether an idle still stands: the latest one, after the user's
468:    * latest message, with no turn running and no message from the gate on its way.
469:    *
470:    * @param s - the session's state.
471:    * @param idle - what the idle saw: its number and the user's message count.
472:    * @returns true when the gate may run, or act on its result.
473:    */
474:   const current = (s, idle) =>
475:     idle.number === s.idles && idle.generation === s.generation && !s.busy && !s.awaiting;
476: 
477:   /**
478:    * Runs the Stop gate for a top-level session that went idle. OpenCode can't
479:    * refuse the end of a turn, so a block starts another one with the gate's
480:    * reasons, as the agent the user picked.
481:    *
482:    * @param id - the session.
483:    * @param idle - the idle's number and the user's message count when it came.
484:    */
485:   const stop = async (id, idle) => {
486:     const s = state(id);
487:     if (!current(s, idle)) {
488:       return; // a later idle, a message or a turn made this one stale
489:     }
490:     if (!s.pending && s.unsent === undefined) {
491:       return; // no message started a turn since the last check: a shell command, a compaction or an abort
492:     }
493:     s.pending = false;
494:     s.running = s.turn;
495:     s.checked = s.activity;
496:     try {
497:       await answer(id, s, idle);
498:     } finally {
499:       s.running = undefined;
500:     }
501:   };
502: 
503:   /**
504:    * Runs the gate for an idle that stands and passes on what it says. A gate
505:    * message that couldn't be sent is sent again instead: the gate already
506:    * counted that attempt.
507:    *
508:    * @param id - the session.
509:    * @param s - its state.
510:    * @param idle - the idle's number and the user's message count when it came.
511:    */
512:   const answer = async (id, s, idle) => {
513:     if (s.unsent !== undefined) {
514:       await deliver(id, s, s.unsent);
515:       return;
516:     }
517:     const result = await hook({ session_id: id, hook_event_name: "Stop", stop_hook_active: s.continued });
518:     // The gate has counted this attempt, so a later idle doesn't make the result stale;
519:     // a message from the user, or a turn that started, does. A turn with no
520:     // message (a shell command) leaves this one's check to the next idle.
521:     if (idle.generation !== s.generation || s.busy || s.awaiting || s.activity !== s.checked) {
522:       if (idle.generation === s.generation) {
523:         s.pending = true;
524:       }
525:       return;
526:     }
527:     if (result.code === 2) {
528:       s.continued = true;
529:       await deliver(id, s, STOP_PREFACE + result.stderr);
530:       return;
531:     }
532:     s.continued = false;
533:     const message = broken(result)
534:       ? `the Stop gate couldn't run: ${result.stderr.trim()}`
535:       : output(result.stdout).systemMessage;
536:     if (message) {
537:       await note(id, message);
538:     }
539:   };
540: 
541:   /**
542:    * Sends the gate's message, which starts another turn. A refused request
543:    * is tried again, up to ATTEMPTS times; one that still fails, or may have
544:    * got through, is kept for the next idle, and dropped if it arrives.
545:    *
546:    * @param id - the session.
547:    * @param s - its state.
548:    * @param text - the message.
549:    */
550:   const deliver = async (id, s, text) => {
551:     const { generation, turn } = s;
552:     s.awaiting = true;
553:     for (let attempt = 0; attempt < ATTEMPTS; attempt += 1) {
554:       const outcome = await send(id, { parts: [{ type: "text", text }] });
555:       if (outcome === "sent") {
556:         s.unsent = undefined;
557:         return;
558:       }
559:       // The user moved on while the request ran, or OpenCode took the message
560:       // anyway (a new turn): sending it again would be stale or a duplicate.
561:       if (generation !== s.generation || turn !== s.turn) {
562:         return;
563:       }
564:       if (outcome === "unknown") {
565:         break; // trying again at once could send it twice
566:       }
567:     }
568:     s.awaiting = false;
569:     s.unsent = text;
570:   };
571: 
572:   return {
573:     event: async ({ event }) => {
574:       if (event.type === "session.created") {
575:         const { id, parentID } = event.properties.info;
576:         if (parentID) {
577:           const top = await root(parentID);
578:           if (top !== undefined) {
579:             parents.set(id, top);
580:           }
581:           return;
582:         }
583:         await start(id, "startup");
584:       } else if (event.type === "session.status") {
585:         const id = event.properties.sessionID;
586:         if (sessions.has(id)) {
587:           // A retry is a turn still running.
588:           const s = state(id);
589:           s.busy = (event.properties.status?.type ?? "idle") !== "idle";
590:           s.activity += s.busy ? 1 : 0;
591:         }
592:       } else if (event.type === "session.error") {
593:         const aborted = event.properties.error?.name === "MessageAbortedError";
594:         if (aborted) {
595:           unresolved.delete(event.properties.sessionID);
596:         }
597:         const s = sessions.get(event.properties.sessionID);
598:         if (s !== undefined) {
599:           s.awaiting = false; // a message that failed after it was accepted
600:           if (aborted) {
601:             s.pending = false; // the user stopped the turn: the gate doesn't send the agent back
602:           }
603:         }
604:       } else if (event.type === "session.idle") {
605:         const id = event.properties.sessionID;
606:         // Before anything waits: later idles and messages make this one stale.
607:         const known = sessions.get(id);
608:         if (known !== undefined && known.running === known.turn && known.activity === known.checked) {
609:           return; // the gate is already answering this turn's idle; after a shell command, this idle checks again
610:         }
611:         const seen = known ? { number: ++known.idles, generation: known.generation } : undefined;
612:         if (known) {
613:           known.busy = false; // now, so activity seen while this handler waits isn't overwritten
614:         }
615:         if ((await root(id)) !== id) {
